title: Slack flows must pass their own egress `source` to SlackIntegration
answers: How do I label Slack API calls by feature?
Why do all Slack calls show source=integration in slack_api_requests_total?
Adding a new Slack notification flow: what source label to use?
body:
Any outbound Slack notification flow that builds a client via `SlackIntegration` should pass its own name: `SlackIntegration(integration, source="<flow>")` (posthog/models/integration/slack.py:SlackIntegration.__init__, keyword-only, default `"integration"`).
- The source is applied to both `.client` and `.async_client(...)`, so sync and async paths of one flow share a label.
- Existing labels: error_tracking_alerts, subscriptions (ee/tasks/subscriptions/slack_subscriptions.py), signals_inbox, signals_scout, stamphog, visual_review, loop_notifications, eval_reports, customer_analytics_event_stream.
- Leave the default `integration` for the Slack app's in-conversation replies and other generic callers.
- Documented in posthog/egress/slack/README.md; update it if the convention changes.
- Test fakes replacing SlackIntegration must accept `source` (products/stamphog/backend/tests/fakes.py:FakeSlackIntegration).
applies: Code that constructs SlackIntegration to send Slack messages from product flows.

Recognized source values include error_tracking_alerts, subscriptions, signals_inbox, signals_scout, stamphog, visual_review, loop_notifications, eval_reports, and customer_analytics_event_stream. Documentation lives in posthog/egress/slack/README.md; update it when the convention changes.
